title: ProofGraph node
description: One axiom, definition, or theorem, together with a proof whose every step carries its own justification. Graph edges are DERIVED from step justifications, never declared by hand.

id.description: Unique within the module. Convention: A* axiom, D* definition, L* background/logical, T* theorem.

kind.description: axiom: assumed, no proof. definition: introduces vocabulary, no proof. background: logical/meta principle assumed by the ambient logic (equality, substitution). theorem: must carry a proof.

natural.description: Precise natural-language statement. Must be unambiguous enough that two mathematicians would formalise it the same way.

context.description: Nodes whose VOCABULARY this statement uses. Distinct from proof dependencies: T4 'inverses are unique' cannot even be stated without A3 (identity) and A4 (inverse), yet its proof may not cite them. These produce 'vocabulary' edges.

strategy.description: One or two sentences of human orientation before the formal steps.

hypotheses.description: Named assumptions discharged by the statement's implication, referable in steps as 'hyp' or 'hyp:name'.

n.description: Presentation ordinal, 1-based and contiguous. NOT stable: inserting a step renumbers everything after it. Never address a step by `n` from outside the proof.

id.description: Immutable identifier, unique within this proof, assigned once and NEVER reused — not even after the step is deleted. This is the only stable address a step has: `T6#collapse-outer`. Choose a name for what the step does, not where it sits.

by.description: Justifications. Each entry is either (a) the id of another node -> becomes a graph edge tagged with this step number, or (b) a LOCAL token that creates no edge: 'hyp', 'hyp:<name>', 's<k>' (an earlier step of this same proof), or 'assumption' inside a subproof.

status.description: draft: contributed, unreviewed. reviewed: two independent human reviewers signed off. verified: a machine proof exists and is linked in `formalization`.

formalization.description: Cross-references into real proof assistants. This is what keeps the project honest: a node claiming 'verified' must point at something a machine checked.

source.description: Where the proof comes from: a textbook, a paper, or 'original'.

assisted_by.description: If an LLM drafted any part of this node, name the model. Required by CONTRIBUTING.md.

note.description: Free prose about the node's status. Exists so that explanations never get smuggled into `formalization`, whose values must stay real declaration names — a prose placeholder there would satisfy the `verified` check without backing it.
